name: Is solid wood or MDF better for kitchen molding and baseboards?

mainEntity.name: Is solid wood or MDF better for kitchen molding and baseboards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Solid wood offers exceptional durability, natural grain patterns, and moisture resistance, whereas MDF (medium-density fiberboard) provides a smooth, cost-effective surface for painted finishes. For kitchens, MDF crown and casing are budget-friendly options that do not warp easily from minor humidity shifts. However, solid wood or polyurethane is often preferred for baseboards near sinks and dishwashers where direct water exposure can cause MDF edges to swell. When coordinating custom finish carpentry with your existing layout, you must weigh whether you plan to stain or paint the moldings, as stained finishes require real hardwood like oak or maple.
acceptedAnswer.description: MDF is cost-effective and ideal for painted crown molding, while solid wood is more durable and water-resistant for baseboards subject to splashes or high foot traffic.
